quizName: Hardest Questions in Missouri Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Pick a helmet that meets DOT and state safety standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Encourage them to take empty roads.

questions.explanation: Do not let anyone ride if they have drunk too much. Stop them from riding by any means, including taking their keys. Help them find another way home.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers will see you.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to know what is behind you. Frequent mirror checks should be part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Eyeballing the tire is a good method.
It is best to squeeze the tire.
Compare the height of the tire to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. An under-inflated tire may look fine, so looking is not enough.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear proper protective clothing when riding. Good protective gear includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: Which of the following types of footwear is best for a motorcycle operator?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or shoes that are high enough to support your ankles provide the best protection. Laced boots are best. If your laces are long, tuck them in before riding.

questions.question: If you are feeling tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope to wake up.
Get off the road and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: If wearing footwear with laces, the laces:

options.text: Should be removed from the footwear.

questions.explanation: Tuck laces securely into your shoes when riding so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight hours, you should:

options.text: Wear bright clothing all the time.
Ride on the shoulder and stay out of traffic.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright clothing to be more visible, even during the day.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose footwear with soles that:

options.text: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
Are made of soft, flimsy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
questions.explanation: Choose boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Pick footwear with soles made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes specifications, how to operate it, and maintenance tips.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery and harder to control on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves when riding.

questions.question: Which organization certifies safe motorcycle helmets?
questions.explanation: Buy a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for maximum protection.

questions.question: Which color makes you easier to see while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green. Bright clothing helps others see you, day or night.

questions.question: What is a danger when riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot
A driver may pull out suddenly into your path
Others may be driving slowly looking for parking

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may pull out suddenly into your path
questions.explanation: A driver may pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: What material are motorcycle riding gloves usually made of?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Should you use a turn signal when it is obvious you are turning?

options.text: No, you do not need to
Yes, you should always use one
Only if there are pedestrians nearby

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you should always use one
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think your turn is obvious. Vehicles you cannot see may be nearby.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the single most effective action to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: How can you reduce head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. It is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see you on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright colors, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: What should proper motorcycle riding clothing cover?

options.text: Your arms completely, but not your legs.
Your legs completely, but not your arms.
Whatever is comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.explanation: For proper protection, wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist constantly watch for on the road ahead?
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for traffic, road hazards, and escape routes. Be ready to react to anything that changes.

questions.question: Which item does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tires, controls, chain, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Even small mechanical problems can be dangerous on a motorcycle.
